summary: Iteration 37 — Telegram consolidation validated. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_37_telegram_consolidation.py with 22 tests, ALL PASS (22/22). Coverage: (1) dedupe sequential — 2nd insert of same update_id returns {status:duplicate}, exactly 1 row in telegram_processed_updates; (2) dedupe concurrent — 2 parallel threads with same update_id → sorted statuses == ['duplicate','ok'], 1 row persisted; (3) update without update_id processes normally; (4) /help command returns 200 and creates command log_event with current_step=/help; (5) system:menu / system:cancel clear active flow state; (6) system:help returns 200; (7) system:back fallback returns 200 when no state; (8) webhook never 500s on crafted edge input (isolation); (9) structural presence of error_id UUID + log_event('message_error'/'callback_error') in routes.py verified; (10) indexes on Mongo verified — telegram_processed_updates.uniq_update_id UNIQUE + ttl_received_at_7d expireAfterSeconds=604800, telegram_alerts_states.uniq_chat_id UNIQUE, telegram_internal_logs.lookup_update_id; (11) _MongoBackedStates SET persists doc (upsert), DEL removes doc, fresh instance ensure_loaded() restores persisted states (simulated restart); (12) regression: menu:pre_ticket, menu:renting, menu:mech_alert, menu:assistencias all still create state with correct active_flow (iteration 32 delegation intact); (13) security: grep for TG token pattern across .md/.py/.js → 0 hits; test_credentials.md contains only '[REDACTED — see BotFather]'; .gitignore includes memory/test_credentials.md; telegram_rollback.md has no real tokens. Also re-ran full iteration_32 suite → 15/15 PASS. Total: 37/37 passing across both suites.
action_items: OPTIONAL / non-blocking: memory/test_credentials.md is present in .gitignore but the file itself is STILL tracked in git history (git ls-files reports it). To fully untrack, main agent should run `git rm --cached memory/test_credentials.md` (as noted by the main agent in the review request). Not a functional issue since tokens are already redacted.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py dedupe pattern (insert-first with UNIQUE + DuplicateKeyError catch) is race-safe and correct; verified end-to-end with concurrent threads.

Update status marker: the insert stores status='processing' then update_one to status='done' after _dispatch_update succeeds. If the dispatcher raises, the doc stays in 'processing' — Telegram won't retry (200 returned) but a monitoring alert on processed_updates.status='processing' age > 5min would catch stuck dispatches. Consider adding to ops runbook.
startup.py ensure_indexes() is idempotent (relies on Mongo's index dedup by name) — restart-safe. Good.

_MongoBackedStates uses asyncio.get_event_loop() which is deprecated in Python 3.12+; on Python 3.11 (current) it still works but emits DeprecationWarning outside a running loop. Consider migrating to asyncio.get_running_loop() with a try/except, or use asyncio.ensure_future in tasks. Not blocking.

The system:back handler currently ALWAYS falls back to main menu (comment says 'Safe fallback: go to menu (per spec, when no safe prior step exists)'). Spec §5 aligns with this, but if the intent is to eventually implement per-flow back stacks, this is where to extend.

log_event 'message_error' / 'callback_error' correctly include error_id (12-char hex) in the `error` field and echo it to the user via {error_id}. Users can quote the reference and admins can grep logs. Good UX.

Minor: two independent 'from pymongo.errors import DuplicateKeyError' + 'from db import db' imports live inside the request handler (line 68-69). Moving them to module scope would save a few microseconds per request but keeps the isolation from bot_api. Cosmetic.

SECURITY: grep across /app for the Telegram token pattern returns 0 matches — the redaction is thorough. .gitignore covers memory/test_credentials.md going forward; main agent should still `git rm --cached` to remove from history (see action_items).
The webhook always returns 200 even on invalid update JSON (parse error) — correct pattern to prevent Telegram retry loops.
